issues.title: Establish the CLI, schemas and deterministic product test harness
scope: Create src/runloc package and a runnable module entry point with help/version/structured errors; do not advertise unimplemented commands as working.
Define versioned config, lease, event and receipt contracts with validated finite budgets and explicit supported platform/profile.
Add scripts/check.py combining repository contract and product unittest discovery; extend hosted Windows/Ubuntu CI with stable named checks and native process-fixture support.
acceptance: Clean source checkout invokes the CLI and documented development commands without hidden installed packages.
Invalid input, unknown schema, unknown command and unimplemented command terminate nonzero with stable redacted JSON errors.
Empty/all-skipped product tests cannot satisfy runtime acceptance; the planning validator remains a separate check.
Required checks run without credentials, QEMU, elevation or external API requests; Python/tooling support and test entry points are documented.
tests: Retained CLI subprocess tests for exit/JSON/help, arbitrary cwd and checkout path containing spaces.
Schema tests for missing/wrong types, negative/nonfinite deadlines, unsupported versions and secret-bearing diagnostics.
Run both README checks and python scripts/check.py; show actual Windows and Ubuntu CI results.
issues.excludes: No VM boot, artifact download, runner registration, GitHub dispatch or product release.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Implement fail-fast host doctor and verified local tool acquisition
scope: Implement doctor with explicit observed host capabilities, headroom, owned paths and exact synthetic key/control-file ACL probes.
Introduce reviewed input locks and local artifact download/extraction/cache adapters for the QEMU toolchain; record provenance and notices.
Handle offline cache, deadlines, archive/path bounds, partial downloads and atomic verified promotion without running a global installer.
acceptance: Unsupported/disabled WHPX is unavailable, not a runtime PASS or implicit TCG selection.
The actual private-file protection sequence works as a standard user on supported Windows; broad explicit ACL fixtures are removed and no SeSecurityPrivilege/elevation is required.
Digest mismatch, malformed/oversized archive, traversal entry and interrupted promotion cannot replace a valid cache.
Doctor is read-only outside synthetic owned fixtures and prints finite resource/download requirements before mutation.
tests: Windows native ACL positive/negative controls, exact failing-path regression inspired by the EzVM pilot and source import checks.
Injected downloader/hash/extractor tests for mismatch, redirect policy, ENOSPC, locked destination, offline valid/invalid cache and interrupted writes.
Construct no real guest in PR CI; opt-in acquisition proof records actual tool identities, exit and hashes.
issues.excludes: No enabling host features, privilege grants, owner-patch import, image build, runner auth or physical WHPX qualification.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Implement lease reservations and one-level disposable QCOW2 storage
scope: Create durable UUID leases, atomic journals/locks and single-guest resource admission using actual CPU/RAM/disk headroom.

Create fresh one-level QCOW2 overlays and seed/control directories from explicit verified base descriptors; use synthetic tiny bases before the later prepared-image issue and validate actual backing metadata.
Implement previewable scoped storage cleanup, sensitive-state marking, reservations and finite retention without deleting live references.
acceptance: Simultaneous controllers cannot reserve the same capacity, port or lease; a rejected reservation makes no partial guest.
Changed/missing/external base, second-level chain, malformed metadata and path escape refuse boot preparation.
Used/job-injected overlays cannot become clean bases or return to a pool; cleanup preserves referenced immutable inputs.
ENOSPC, journal failure, moved cold root and stale lock recovery retain truth and previous valid state; unresolved ownership holds capacity visibly.
tests: Real file-lock/process race tests and fake-clock/resource tests for oversubscription and lease reuse refusal.
Synthetic qemu-img fixtures for backing/format/relocation plus bounded real tiny-image checks with verified tools.
Traversal/junction/hardlink, live base reference, failed atomic replace and disk-full negative controls; assert unrelated sentinel files survive.
issues.excludes: No guest execution, registered-runner pool, external API calls or general image portability product.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Own QEMU launch, QMP and bounded Windows process lifetime
scope: Implement explicit WHPX argument arrays, controller-owned QMP stdio, independent serial capture and concurrent bounded stream drains.
Contain QEMU before execution with a proved Windows ownership primitive; record executable/creation/root identity and durable lease association.
Implement status/graceful stop/contained termination with deadlines and quarantine on ambiguity.
acceptance: Start returns on the intended readiness boundary without waiting for a long-lived child to close captured pipes.
Supervisor death terminates its contained process tree; a reused PID or unrelated same-name process is never stopped.
WHPX launch does not silently fall back; unsupported containment or requested accelerator fails closed before useful execution.
No guest-reachable QMP TCP endpoint, host share or leaked process handle; stop confirms owned exit before releasing storage.
tests: Native Windows lightweight process tests: captured start, descendant holding pipe, suspended containment, timeout, abrupt supervisor exit and handle lifetime.
PID reuse/executable/root mismatch negative controls with unrelated process sentinel surviving.
QMP protocol/error/EOF/output-flood tests and a bounded real disposable WHPX boot/stop smoke; mocked arguments are not physical execution proof.
issues.excludes: No owner VM control, blanket process kill, host service, nested virtualization or Linux/KVM support.
issues.prerequisites: Native Windows process tests can run hosted without QEMU; the separate boot smoke needs an approved WHPX host and accepted image.

issues.title: Build and qualify a credential-free Linux runner image recipe
scope: Implement image build/inspect with pinned Ubuntu 24.04 x64 input, explicit guest packages and official runner dependencies/archive.
Build in an owned bounded VM, sanitize identity and credentials, cleanly stop, validate and atomically publish base+manifest.
Record exact inputs, recipe, resulting digest, runner-version freshness and supported shell-action tool profile; add notices and rebuild procedure.
acceptance: A verified reusable base has no registration, JIT configuration, repository worktree, private keys, job state or reused lease machine identity.
Failed or interrupted build cannot overwrite the previous valid base or publish a partially prepared image.
Actual guest inspection demonstrates the declared tools/dependencies and unprivileged runner user; no Docker/sudo parity claim.
Base inspection rejects unknown recipe/version/digest and moving unpinned acquisition; image metadata is sufficient to reproduce or explain an unavailable upstream input.
tests: Recipe/manifest validation, missing/mismatched inputs, build timeout/failed provision/failed shutdown and atomic-promotion negative tests.
A bounded real disposable image build plus offline secret/identity inspection, with exact source/tool/image evidence and cleanup.
Retained sanitize regressions and fresh-boot identity controls; keep fixture keys synthetic and never export a credentialed disk.
issues.excludes: No registered runner, GitHub job, persistent developer profile, Windows media or broad hosted-image equivalence.
issues.prerequisites: Supported Windows/WHPX host and explicitly selected download sources; if unavailable keep physical image acceptance open, not mocked green.

issues.title: Establish authenticated per-lease guest readiness and control
scope: Create per-lease seed/SSH identity and a small versioned Linux control wrapper for readiness, configuration, runner status and collection.
Bind SSH host trust to fresh lease/nonce/image identity through captured bootstrap serial evidence; use isolated known_hosts.
Transfer sensitive one-use configuration through authenticated stdin/file into mode0600 tmpfs, with bounded operations and redaction.
acceptance: Guest readiness requires correct completed provisioning, lease nonce/image, owned QEMU and authenticated channel, not an open port/printed marker.
Wrong/stale key, nonce, seed or partial provisioning refuses credentials and runner startup.
No private host SSH/API secret or JIT data appears in serial, argv, base or normal receipt; guest output cannot choose arbitrary host export paths.
Guest control runs in the documented unprivileged profile and reports precise timeout/transport/command failures.
tests: Stale/forged READY, wrong host key, reboot, partial provision, lost SSH and oversized output negative controls.
Synthetic-secret inspection across transfer/success/error/collection paths; hostile collection filename cannot write outside lease export.
Real fresh-guest readiness, fixed control operation and cleanup with separate host/guest evidence.
issues.excludes: No GitHub registration, arbitrary interactive terminal injection, trust-on-first-use bypass or host folder mount.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Implement host-only GitHub auth and repository-scoped JIT runners
scope: Implement credential-provider and documented GitHub REST boundaries with pinned API semantics, finite requests and injected fixtures.
Acquire repository-scoped JIT configuration only for a ready owned guest and register a unique Linux/X64/profile/lease identity.
Observe runner readiness and exact-ID removal; keep remote cleanup uncertainty and sensitive payloads out of durable/public state.
acceptance: Host authorization never enters guest/base/logs; guest receives only its single-use capability via the accepted006 channel.
Unique runner ID/name/label/repository association is verified; generic self-hosted routing is insufficient.
Accepted-but-response-lost registration is reconciled before retry, preventing duplicate runners; permissions and rate limits fail clearly.
Observed one-job registration and deregistration are distinct from VM disposal; network errors never prove absence or success.
tests: Recorded synthetic fixtures for success, timeout-after-accept,429/Retry-After,401/403/404/409/5xx, pagination and stale/incorrect identity.
Secret redaction and no-credential-call unit CI; exact-ID deletion cannot remove another runner sentinel.
Explicitly approved live test-repository registration/online/removal proof with API IDs and guest-channel evidence; no real job required yet.
issues.excludes: No PAT enrollment, org-wide fleet, runner service on host, public-fork trigger or runner-protocol implementation.
issues.prerequisites: Existing host auth/App with repository administration capability and an approved qualification repository (techrote/runloc is the intended test repository); no production secrets.

issues.title: Orchestrate one real job through collection and complete disposal
scope: Implement foreground plan/run/status/stop/reconcile single-lease supervisor and phase deadlines, using accepted adapters.
Bind an approved workflow definition/candidate/job to the unique ready runner; persist external write intent and observed IDs.
Collect bounded redacted diagnostics, cancel only owned work when needed, terminate VM and remove local sensitive state with explicit remote cleanup obligations.
acceptance: An actual approved Linux job completes on its assigned unique runner and is associated with exact candidate, workflow/run/job/attempt and lease.
A deliberately failing job remains a failed outcome even when cleanup succeeds; runner-online/guest PASS/exit without API conclusion cannot substitute.
One used VM never accepts a second job; overlay/seed/control keys disappear after confirmed QEMU exit and registration disposition is known.
Controller restart, cancellation, collection failure and cleanup API outage reconcile without re-executing a job or losing the original cause; unresolved state is quarantined.
tests: State-machine/fake-clock tests at every transition and exact phase timeout; failed-job and queue expiry controls.
Real one-job success plus failed job with QEMU exit, disk/seed/key removal, API conclusion and exact runner disposition evidence.
Two successive fresh leases prove distinct identity and no sentinel carry-over; second-job scheduling cannot use the first runner.
issues.excludes: No multi-guest pool, autoscaling, gate promotion, broad workflow trust or success based only on logs.
issues.prerequisites: Accepted physical adapters and explicit host authorization for the trusted qualification workflow; ordinary PR tests remain fully offline.

issues.title: Expose bounded evidence receipts and read-only terminal performance stats
scope: Implement versioned evidence snapshots/events, allowed export manifest, logs and read-only stats commands.
Measure phase wall times, host process/resource use, queue/run IDs and cleanup obligations with source/freshness labels.
Bound sampling/history/log size/retention and preserve useful diagnostics independently of guest survival.
acceptance: Stats reads actual supervisor/API/host state without mutation, duplicate runner sessions or extending lifetime.
Cold acquisition/build, integrity validation, boot/readiness, API queue, job, collection and disposal are measured separately.
Unknown/stale values are visibly unknown/stale, CPU denominator and sampling interval are recorded, guest claims are distinguished.
Export contains no disks/JIT/keys/API credentials and is byte/hash traceable to source evidence; interrupted monitor cannot change a job outcome.
tests: Fake-clock and counter tests, stale/missing snapshots, concurrent atomic writes, corrupt journal and unsupported metrics.
Output flood/history/retention limits, synthetic secret filtering and malicious export-path/manifest controls.
Real read-only stats during an approved008 lease, checking process association and no extra lifecycle writes.
issues.excludes: No AI-model metrics, tiled dashboard, input terminal, GPU monitoring or assertion that monitoring is independent qualification.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Dispatch independent hosted/private comparisons with offline fallback
scope: Implement compare preview/dispatch and reviewed hosted/private workflow templates for identical Linux workloads.
Dispatch hosted first, then optionally reserve/ready an owned VM and target its unique label; correlate both attempt/run identities.
Implement finite private queue monitoring, exact-run cancellation and response-lost reconciliation while hosted remains independent.
acceptance: Offline/busy/disabled/unsupported/private boot/API failure cannot prevent or cancel accepted hosted execution.
Both runs bind exact same candidate/input recipe/comparison ID and independently observed definition/profile/host identities.
Workflow ref and candidate SHA are not confused; mutable-ref movement or mismatched assigned runner invalidates private evidence.
Private disappearance after dispatch is bounded by controller queue TTL, not job timeout; controller-offline uncertainty is visible and reconciled on restart.
Dispatch response loss cannot duplicate hosted/private runs; no automatic first-green cancellation or required-check policy change.
tests: Stub call order/count tests and real adapters for documented successful dispatch response shapes, timeouts and run-ID reconciliation.
Offline before/after readiness,429,permission failure,ref movement,wrong runner,duplicate intent and cancel-wrong-run negative controls.
Live paired approved Linux workflow run with same candidate, result assertions and evidence; hosted continues after intentionally unavailable private lane.
issues.excludes: No required matrix private leg, public PR auto-registration, production branch-rule edit or Windows/Linux equivalence claim.
issues.prerequisites: Reviewed templates available on default branch, existing Actions write auth and explicit trusted qualification repository; unit tests never dispatch workflows.

issues.title: Qualify crash recovery, cancellation and failure cleanup
scope: Add a bounded fault-injection qualification runner and recovery matrix covering each durable transition/ambiguous external-write window.
Exercise native containment, storage/credential/API obligations, queue disappearance, log flood and resource errors.
Repair narrowly evidenced integration defects, retaining original failure records and explicit cleanup/quarantine outcomes.
acceptance: Controller death before/after registration/dispatch and during running/collection leaves no unowned active VM or reused used lease.
Restart does not repeat completed/unknown external actions blindly; remote uncertainty and capacity obligations remain visible.
Job failure/cancellation/timeout and disk/log/transport failures never become success from cleanup or a skipped check.
Unrelated QEMU/process/file/runner sentinels survive all recovery operations, including PID reuse and path reparse cases.
The report distinguishes deterministic unit faults, native process proofs and real VM/API scenarios; physical gates remain open if missing.
tests: Native Windows controller/child-pipe kill, reused PID, containment failure and owned scope tests.
ENOSPC at download/journal/collection/promotion, wrong identity, log flood, API outage/removal failure and host-restart reconciliation simulations.
At least real controller-death during one guest lease, failed-job disposal and offline-after-private-dispatch proof using approved test assets.
issues.excludes: No escape testing, owner infrastructure disruption, wildcard cleanup, hypervisor tuning or broad rewrite unrelated to observed defects.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Run the clean timed WHPX pilot and publish a go/no-go assessment
scope: Commit a qualification plan with workload/parity assertions, resource/cache/network conditions and numerical acceptance targets before any timed trial.
Run clean cold/warm Windows/WHPX Linux-job trials with independent hosted Linux reference and complete failure/disposal evidence.
Analyze phase costs and measured bottlenecks, repair small proved defects and publish reproducible receipts plus an explicit qualification decision.
acceptance: At least 3 trials per declared cold/warm mode use fresh leases and exact controller/candidate/definition/input identities, with all samples retained.
Actual WHPX execution, GitHub job assertions, registration disposition and local disposal are independently observed; detection/configured accel is insufficient.
Report median/range and cold/warm phase breakdown, not unsupported p95 or borrowed EzVM Windows timings.
Zero false success/leaked/second-job runners,3/3 clean leases per accepted mode, failure cleanup and predeclared timing/resource targets determine go/no-go.
A no-go is reported honestly and keeps physical product/release gates open until repaired or explicitly revised; no permanent runner registration to disguise failure.
tests: Negative-control checks invalidate incomplete logs, wrong source/recipe/accelerator, mismatched guest OS or failed workload despite fast wall time.
Replay receipts through assessment code and compare against known pass/fail boundary fixtures.
Full approved physical/API pilot, including standard-user exact ACL preflight, verified source cleanliness and actual complete end markers.
issues.excludes: No self-granted privileges, host setting changes, owner-patch copy, Windows nested-WHPX claim or required-gate promotion.
issues.prerequisites: Approved Windows/WHPX hardware, accepted image/adapters, configured test-repository auth and numerical targets written before measurement. If unavailable publish a blocked report and keep this issue open.

issues.title: Package the CLI and document a clean on-demand runner quickstart
scope: Create source/wheel or equally small installable Python package, locked metadata, notices and supported-platform statement.
Document clean setup/doctor/image/auth-preview/run/stats/disposal/recovery with reviewed workflow examples.
Verify updates/rollback/retention/uninstall leave other projects and running immutable inputs untouched; provide precise space/download/capability estimates.
acceptance: A clean directory/user development environment reproduces the accepted shell-action runner using only documented steps and existing approved auth.
Package contains own source/schemas/recipes/notices and no runtime disks, keys, seeded media, tokens, QEMU installer or guest archive.
MIT scope and third-party source/distribution notices are accurate; no code copied from EzVM without explicit compatible terms.
Examples target the real unique lease labels and approved candidate/definition inputs; installing/viewing docs never registers or dispatches.
Update/rebuild of stale runner images and rollback preserve running leases and prior valid cache; uninstall is exact-scope and previewable.
tests: Package file-content/metadata tests plus fresh venv smoke from built distribution rather than source import.
Synthetic secret/binary exclusion, clean path with spaces, interrupted update and unrelated installation sentinel controls.
Documented real one-job quickstart replay with receipt IDs and complete disposal, reusing unchanged qualified tree evidence only when identity is proved.
issues.excludes: No bundled proprietary Windows image, global install/service, broad redistribution assumption or one-click claim hiding credentials/features.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Close the v0.1 release gate with whole-programme evidence
scope: Audit every001–013 clause against actual main implementation/tests/merged PRs and immutable runtime evidence.
Resolve narrow release blockers, rerun changed-tree tests and qualify clean package plus recovery/upgrade behavior.
Publish tagged release/source package with platform/profile matrix, measured results, limitations, provenance and validated evidence index.
acceptance: All001–013 issues are genuinely accepted on main and relevant required automated head/post-merge checks are green.
Physical012 go decision, repeated clean leases, failed-job cleanup and controller restart recovery are complete and source-bound.
No skipped hardware requirement, stale head, unresolved cleanup, fabricated benchmark or unreviewed owner patch is included.
Release contents/SBOM/notices and fresh install/upgrade/rollback instructions match the tested package; Windows guest/KVM extensions stay unsupported.
Final review findings are resolved or explicitly scoped limitations; source tag and published artifacts are verified after release.
tests: Machine-readable acceptance index checks missing/duplicate evidence, wrong source/recipe identities and unresolved gated issues.
Package-level clean reproduction plus required failure/regression suites; no unchanged full pilot rerun just for prose.
Verify main/post-merge and tag/artifact digests, document actual release checks and known limitations.
issues.excludes: No automatic delivery of015–019, private acceptance promotion, scope substitution or release when physical evidence is unavailable.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Add a bounded foreground multi-lease queue and resource admission
scope: Extend the accepted one-lease controller with explicit max guests, CPU/RAM/disk reservations, fair bounded queue, admission pause and drain.
Keep per-lease one-job identity, registration, deadlines, metrics and cleanup independent across concurrent guests.
Expose predicted capacity/queue and reject oversubscription without changing host/owner VM allocations.
acceptance: At least 2 independent approved jobs can run concurrently only when actual configured headroom allows; default remains1.
Pause stops new admission, drain finishes/cleans existing leases, cancel targets an exact queue item without deleting another.
Crash/restart, capacity loss and quarantine cannot free resources incorrectly or duplicate jobs.
No warmed registered guest or used-overlay reuse; per-lease disposal and source binding remain intact.
Measured concurrent/sequential trials report contention and limits, not throughput inferred from configured slots.
tests: Concurrent process-lock/reservation and fairness/starvation tests with fake clocks and resource pressure.
Two real fresh guests/jobs plus one failure or cancellation demonstrate isolation, no contamination and full cleanup.
Queue restart, ENOSPC, exhausted RAM, pending remote removal and wrong-ID cancel negative controls.
issues.excludes: No remote fleet, permanent service, public autoscaling webhook or unbounded job admission.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Evaluate Windows guest runners and nested-virtualization limits
scope: Produce a bounded feasibility study for Windows GitHub runner guests, supported/licensed media and unattended unique disposable image recipe.
Separate ordinary Windows jobs from Windows jobs that themselves require WHPX/nested virtualization; evaluate actual platform constraints.
Define a follow-up implementation plan or evidenced no-go, with measured costs and no unsupported support labels.
acceptance: Report explicitly separates host OS, guest OS, job platform, acceleration and any nested requirements.
Media acquisition/distribution/licensing prerequisites are documented; no unauthorized proprietary image redistribution or silent host change.
If an approved image is available, a bounded disposable ordinary Windows job has actual evidence; nested WHPX is separately tested or explicitly unsupported.
If prerequisites or nested support are absent, a reviewed no-go/blocked feasibility outcome can close this research issue without claiming product support.
Any proposed implementation is new bounded issues with tests, not an unreviewed extension enabled during the spike.
tests: Decision matrix and evidence validation reject Linux-as-Windows or capability-detection-as-execution claims.
Optional real licensed Windows image/job experiment has explicit source/profile/cleanup receipts and finite bounds.
Document reproducible negative evidence and exact follow-up gates for any unsupported case.
issues.excludes: No assumption that the original EzVM Windows qualification now works inside a Linux or Windows guest; no production feature promise.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Qualify a Linux/KVM host backend with the same lease contract
scope: Implement optional Linux x64/KVM doctor/process/locking/permission adapters while preserving the shared CLI/lease/evidence interfaces.
Use a native owned process/session relationship, QMP and explicit KVM with the accepted Linux guest profile.
Add platform-specific qualification and documentation without replacing Windows/WHPX coverage.
acceptance: KVM permission or capability failure is explicit, with no privilege install or implicit TCG fallback.
Owned process identity/death/recovery and single-job disposal match existing invariants under native Linux tests.
Actual Linux/KVM job/cleanup receipts prove support; Ubuntu hosted unit CI alone does not.
Windows required tests remain green and Linux-specific paths do not regress Windows path/ACL behavior.
One platform cannot satisfy a missing qualification gate for another.
tests: Native Linux process-group/start-time/signal and lock tests, reused PID and unrelated sentinel controls.
Real bounded KVM Linux job and failure cleanup on approved hardware, recorded separately from WHPX.
Shared conformance suite and CLI schema parity across both hosts.
issues.excludes: No rootless-container replacement, host service, GPU device passthrough or automatic device-permission changes.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Evaluate official scale-set integration and future CI-provider adapters
scope: Evaluate the official GitHub scale-set client/ARC fit before extending manual dispatch to autoscaling.
Document the minimal runner-provider interface and an optional signed-event/polling design that preserves local admission and cleanup.
Deliver a small isolated feasibility prototype or explicit no-go plus scoped implementation issues; keep deployed v0.1 behavior unchanged.
acceptance: Compare supported official approaches, permissions, operational footprint and queue semantics using current primary references.
No custom undocumented runner protocol, Kubernetes requirement or public inbound listener is introduced as a default.
Duplicate/out-of-order events, lost acknowledgements, offline host and unavailable capacity have concrete decision/test contracts.
Other CI-provider exploration does not weaken GitHub job/credential/source association or claim an implemented provider.
A reviewed evidence-backed go/no-go completes the research issue; production autoscaling requires separate implementation acceptance.
tests: Synthetic signed-event/replay/order/expiry/admission fixtures and permission-failure tests in an isolated prototype.
Provider-contract comparison verifies at-most-one execution, evidence identity and teardown obligations.
Record actual prototype limitations and bounded follow-up tasks; no live production registration.
issues.excludes: No unattended webhook deployment, auto-enrollment of admin credentials, multi-host fleet or promise that a spike is a production feature.
issues.prerequisites: None beyond accepted dependencies and ordinary local development tools.

issues.title: Design and qualify private-result promotion with hosted fallback
scope: Specify one stable required acceptance check which may use qualified equivalent private results while hosted continues/falls back.
Bind trusted controller evidence to exact candidate, workflow definition, recipe/profile and actual private job/disposal; define finite decision and failure semantics.
Implement only after explicit repository policy authorization and demonstrated equivalent results/performance; migrate requirements transparently with rollback.
acceptance: An offline/failed/unqualified private attempt cannot strand the required gate or suppress meaningful hosted failure.
Forged guest PASS, wrong candidate, reused receipt, different platform/tool profile or stale workflow definition cannot satisfy the gate.
Host/controller outage and delayed/duplicate results have deterministic timeout/fallback behavior; a fast missing/failed assertion is never accepted.
Branch-rule/check-policy changes are previewed, reviewed and explicitly authorized, not an installation side effect.
Real equivalent-workload tests show shorter accepted completion where justified, while known failing cases remain failures; comparison-only mode remains available.
tests: Truth-table/state tests for both lanes success/failure/cancel/timeout/offline/race, mismatched source/recipe and spoofed/replayed evidence.
Staging repository end-to-end gate checks with exact statuses/permissions and rollback; ordinary PR CI cannot access admin credentials.
Publish measured merge-wait comparison, parity evidence and failure cases before enabling production policy.
issues.excludes: No first-green-wins shortcut, silent branch-protection bypass, generic all-checks assertion or Windows/Linux result substitution.
issues.prerequisites: The owner must authorize the concrete required-check policy for the target repository; until then complete a reviewable staging design/PR without changing production requirements.
